brief: Goldman's Cullen Morgan recaps positioning metrics as of September 28, 2026. CTAs are estimated long $72bn of global equities (54th percentile) and are modeled to buy roughly $11.5bn over the next week in a flat tape, scaling to $20.25bn over a month. A down-tape scenario flips them to sellers of $15.81bn over one week or $157.78bn over one month. US pensions are modeled to sell $33bn of US equities, ranking in the 97th percentile of three-year estimates and the 98th percentile since 2000. GS Prime Brokerage data show book leverage ticking down while global equities were net sold for the first time in five weeks. Industrials led selling, driven by shorts. Financials led European buying, driven by longs. Health Care was net sold for a sixth straight week and Info Tech was net bought for a fourth straight week, though the pace of buying moderated. About 87% of SPX corporates are in blackout, rising to 93% by week's end. Key SPX pivots are 7665 short term, 7444 medium term, and 6972 long term. The note reports these metrics without arguing a directional thesis.
